subject: No mediation effect in multigroup model

messages.author: d4c32e52e290d408
messages.subject: No mediation effect in multigroup model
parts:
Hello everyone!

I am fitting the data now to a single-level model which works fine except from one thing: when I include the group argument in the sem-function, the mediation effect is not significant in one group although in this group the a-path and the b-path have been significant (when I do not group the data, it does work).

On the SEMNET-list, someone suggested bootstrapping after multiple imputation but I have a couple of missings and no normality in my data. Therefore, I went with the MLR-estimator and FIML for missings by now. Also, to be honest, I have no experience with bootstrapping or MI. Therefore, I was wondering how to do that or if there is an easier way to deal with this problem?

Maybe also something is weird in the syntax (see below)? Moreover, it is possible to establish measurement invariance accross groups but when I clude "intercept" in the group.equal-argument, it says that eignevalues are to small.

Thank you in advance!

Best regards,

Franzi

d.gran.sem1.tot <- '#measurement model
K1 =~ RF1K1 + RF1K2 + RF1K3 + RF1K4
RL1 =~ RF1RL1 + RF1RL2 + RF1RL3 + RF1RL4 + RF1RL5
IE2 =~ RF2IE1 + RF2IE2 + RF2IE3

#structural model
##a-paths
K1 ~ c(dak1, mak1)*diss1 + c(dak2,mak2)*g.div_hk1             #d = group 1; m = group 2
RL1 ~ c(dar1, mar1)*diss1 + c(dar2, mar2)*g.div_hk1
##direct effects (c1) & b-paths
IE2 ~ c(dci1, mci1)*diss1 + c(dci2, mci2)*g.div_hk1 + c(dbik, mbik)*K1  + c(dbir, mbir)*RL1

##correlations & residual covariances between latent mediators
diss1 ~~ g.div_hk1      #IVs: manifest
K1 ~~ RL1               #mediators: allowed to covary

#indirect & total effects
##specific indirect effects for group 1
di.dis.ko.str := dak1*dbik
di.div.ko.str := dak2*dbik
di.dis.rl.str := dar1*dbir
di.div.rl.str := dar2*dbir
##average indirect effect of both mediators
dav.i.dis.str := ((dak1*dbik) + (dar1*dbir))/2
dav.i.div.str := ((dak2*dbik) + (dar2*dbir))/2
##total effects of combined mediators
dt.dis.str := (dak1*dbik) + (dar1*dbir) + dci1  
dt.div.str := (dak2*dbik) + (dar2*dbir) + dci2

##specific indirect effects for group 2
mi.dis.ko.str := mak1*mbik
mi.div.ko.str := mak2*mbik
mi.dis.rl.str := mar1*mbir
mi.div.rl.str := mar2*mbir
##average indirect effect
mav.i.dis.str := ((mak1*mbik) + (mar1*mbir))/2
mav.i.div.str := ((mak2*mbik) + (mar2*mbir))/2
##total effects of combined mediators
mt.dis.str := (mak1*mbik) + (mar1*mbir) + mci1   
mt.div.str := (mak2*mbik) + (mar2*mbir) + mci2'

tot.d <- sem(d.gran.sem1.tot, fin.set3,
             estimator = "ML",  
             fixed.x = F,        
             missing = "FIML",
             group = "v_djn", group.equal = c("loadings"))
summary(tot.d, fit.measures = T, standardized = T,rsquare = T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: No mediation effect in multigroup model
parts: I have no experience with bootstrapping or MI.
That's rough, and probably not worth the effort:  https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2013.816235
if there is an easier way to deal with this problem?

The default delta method with robust SEs should provide sufficient Type I error control.  You can see the ?runMI help page in the semTools package for examples of how to fit your lavaan model to multiple imputations.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: No mediation effect in multigroup model
parts: Just to make sure I got it, does this approach sound like a good idea to you?

I don't know what MedPow is, but if you want to use the Monte Carlo approach, that is a good option, and there is a semTools function to help out:

?monteCarloMed

For the ACM= argument, you just need the vcov(fit) output
So you suggest that I should go with the default values instead of MI+BS?
Regardless of whether you use MI, bootstrapping does not necessarily give you much better CIs than the delta method or Monte Carlo CIs.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: No mediation effect in multigroup model
parts: would you say the resulting CIs are more useful than the CIs resulting from the delta method?
They should be (asymptotically) equivalent, but as sample size increases from small to moderate, I would expect the Monte Carlo approach to start being trustworthy sooner than the delta method.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: No mediation effect in multigroup model
parts:
For a comparison of the delta method and Monte Carlo CIs (along with bootstrapping) see Preacher & Selig (2012). With smaller sample sizes and smaller effect sizes the Monte Carlo CI does out perform the delta method.

http://www.quantpsy.org/pubs/preacher_selig_2012.pdf
